questions.q: What does enabling Container Insights on an AKS cluster actually deploy?
options: A separate Kubernetes cluster dedicated only to monitoring
The Azure Monitor agent as a containerized DaemonSet running on every node, shipping data to a Log Analytics workspace
A SQL Server instance inside the cluster for log storage
Nothing — Container Insights only reads data AKS already stores by default
questions.explain: Container Insights deploys the Azure Monitor agent as a DaemonSet on every node, collecting performance, inventory, and log data and shipping it to a Log Analytics workspace.

questions.q: Which table would you query to find pods stuck in a `Pending` or `Failed` state, by namespace?
options: KubePodInventory
ContainerLogV2
Heartbeat
AzureActivity
questions.explain: KubePodInventory records every pod's phase (Running, Pending, Failed), namespace, and scheduled node — exactly what that health-check query needs.

questions.q: What does `ContainerLogV2` carry, and how is it different from the older `ContainerLog`?
options: It stores only Kubernetes events, never container output
It is a metrics table, not a log table, unlike ContainerLog
It only exists for Windows node pools
It carries stdout/stderr from every container, using the current, more efficient schema that replaces the older ContainerLog table
questions.explain: ContainerLogV2 is the current schema for container stdout/stderr collection, more efficient than the older ContainerLog table it replaces.

questions.q: What does Container Insights' Live Data feature give you that a KQL query cannot?
options: A permanently stored archive of every container's logs for one year
Automatic cost reduction on Log Analytics ingestion
Real-time pod logs, events, and exec access in the Azure portal, without needing a local kubectl session first
A way to run T-SQL instead of KQL against the workspace
questions.explain: Live Data streams logs, events, and exec access directly in the portal in close to real time, the AKS equivalent of Application Insights' Live Metrics — a live view with no query needed first.

questions.q: Why is Container Insights specifically called out as a FinOps concern in this lesson?
options: Because ContainerLogV2 and high-cardinality Perf data can drive significant Log Analytics ingestion cost if every container's verbose output is collected at full fidelity on every node
Because AKS clusters cannot run without Container Insights enabled
Because Container Insights is billed separately from Log Analytics regardless of data volume
Because data collection rules only apply to Application Insights, not Container Insights
questions.explain: Container Insights is one of the most common drivers of Log Analytics ingestion cost, which is why data collection rules exist to scope exactly what gets collected — a decision that sits between this chapter and the course's later FinOps material.
